rules.title: Prohibition on Sale or Provision of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley 
landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

rules.title: Prohibition on Landlord Use of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from using a coordinated pricing algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. Each separate month a violation continues and each separate residential dwelling unit for which the algorithm was used constitutes a distinct violation.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley. Each separate month that a violation exists or continues, and each 
separate residential dwelling unit for which the landlord used the coordinated pricing 
algorithm, shall constitute a separate and distinct violation.

rules.title: Tenant Private Right of Action and Remedies for Coordinated Pricing Algorithm Violations
rules.requirement: An aggrieved tenant may file a civil action against a landlord for violations of section 13.63.030(B) for injunctive relief, money damages, and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. The court must award reasonable attorney's fees and costs to the tenant if the tenant prevails.
rules.quoted_span:
An aggrieved tenant may file a civil action for violations of section 13.63.030, 
subsection B, for injunctive relief, money damages, and/or civil penalties of up to $1,000 
per violation. The court shall award reasonable attorney’s fees and costs to the tenant if 
the tenant is the prevailing party in such a civil action.

rules.title: Unenforceability of Lease Provisions Restricting Prevailing Tenant Attorney's Fees
rules.requirement: Any lease provision that limits a prevailing tenant from recovering attorney's fees is unenforceable against a tenant's claim for attorney's fees arising under subsection 13.63.040(B).
rules.quoted_span:
A lease provision that limits a 
prevailing tenant from obtaining attorneys’ fees shall not be enforceable against a 
tenant’s claim for attorneys’ fees that arises under this subsection 13.63.040(B).
